newsitem.title: USA: Air travel carries Florida to tourism record.
newsitem.headline: Air travel carries Florida to tourism record.

text.p: A boost in air travel helped Florida set a tourism record, with an unprecedented 43 million visitors traveling to the state in 1996, state officials said Thursday.
The total represents a 4.2 percent increase over 1995, according to the Florida Tourism Industry Marketing Corp, the public-private agency that promotes Florida's visitor industry.

Industry euphoria about the report was tempered by the threat of an American Airlines strike. American is a dominant carrier in Florida, accounting for 52 percent of flights through Miami International Airport.
The tourism group said air travel has played a growing role in Florida's visitor industry, surpassing auto travel to the state by widening margins for the past three years.
The number of travelers reaching Florida by air soared to 23.5 million in 1996, a 9.3 percent over the previous year. The number arriving by auto dipped by 1.4 percent to 19.5 million for the year.

Year-end financial data were still pending. But the corporation said that through November, tax revenues from tourism and recreational sales were $34.2 billion, a seven percent increase over the same period in 1996.
The corporation attributed Florida's banner tourism year to the strong economy, cheap air fares, a favorable exchange rate, and bitter cold weather in the U.S. Midwest.
The state's theme parks also added several new attractions, while Walt Disney World, one of Florida's most popular destinations, held a heavily promoted 25th anniversary celebration.
Concerns about crime have also eased since the series of brutal and highly publicized tourist killings that plagued Florida's tourism industry three years ago.
